key_insight: CNeVA learns a per-agent behavior latent from discounted returns, enabling realistic traffic simulation that can be steered along interpretable axes such as speed, acceleration, safety, and map compliance.
engineering_relevance: This makes it useful for autonomous driving validation because engineers can reproduce edge cases, isolate variables, and test policies under controlled, risk-free scenario changes.
method: Infers a Gaussian behavior latent with a closed-form conjugate variational update from per-channel discounted returns.
Uses a rectified-flow trajectory generator trained with mixed channel-mask curriculum and classifier-free guidance.
Introduces soft eligibility gates with smooth exponential decay to preserve gradient signal when reward data are sparse.
evidence_signal: On the Waymo Open Motion Dataset, the method achieves competitive realism while showing monotone controllability for speed and acceleration, with improved safety controllability under soft eligibility.
watch_item: Steering metrics must be checked against physical-plausibility guardrails because controllability can be confounded by reward hacking or stall-like artifacts.
paper_title: Controllable Sim Agents with Behavior Latents
